mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.25% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO < -1% monthly change.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which raises real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above their 12-month averages signals robust demand growth, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and GDPC1 exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month average for five consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month average for five consecutive months.
